_about: HAND-AUTHORED SYNTHETIC FIXTURE for the LIVE row read (no GSVTK_ENTITY_JSON). Every value is a
PLACEHOLDER: the attributes on a real GATK-SV row are object paths, and this repo's publish audit
red-flags those, so the fixture states NAMES bound to placeholder strings and the legs grade names.
These scenarios answer `fapi.get_entity` -- the point lookup -- not a listing. The tool used to walk
`terra.entity_sample()` pages because terra/terra.py had no attribute-level reader; it now calls
`terra.entity_attributes()`, which is one GET and returns the row's attributes, None for a 404, and
raises for anything else. The five scenarios are the five ways that endpoint can answer:
row-found          200, attributes at the top level           -> PRESENT / PRESENT-EMPTY per name
row-found-nested   200 with the same body nested under `entity` -> the SAME tally: a21cb3b's lesson
present-empty      200, attributes is {}                       -> bound-to-nothing, not absence
row-gone           404                                         -> ABSENT, the only arm allowed to say it
body-no-attributes 200 with no attributes member at all        -> UNKNOWN, and not 'binds nothing'
`row-gone` and `lookup-500` are separate scenarios with separate legs because both mean 'do not
guess' for opposite reasons, and collapsing them is how a check starts manufacturing missing inputs.
